title: Tiliroside attenuates acute kidney injury by inhibiting ferroptosis through the disruption of NRF2-KEAP1 interaction.
authors: Cai, Fangfang; Li, Dangran; Zhou, Kaiqian; Zhang, Wen; Yang, Yunwen
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物tiliroside通过破坏NRF2-KEAP1蛋白互作抑制铁死亡以缓解急性肾损伤，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作和分子对接，但核心是PPI而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent process that regulates cell death. Emerging evidences suggest that ferroptosis induces acute kidney injury (AKI) progression, and inhibiting ferroptosis provides an effect strategy for AKI treatment. The disruption of the NRF2-KEAP1 protein to protein interaction (PPI) induces NRF2 activation, which provides a promising strategy that can identify new ferroptosis inhibitors. A previous study revealed that tiliroside, a glycosidic flavonoid extracted from Edgeworthia chrysantha Lindl (buds), has anti-neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective effects via NRF2 activation. However, the mechanism through which tiliroside activates NRF2 is unknown, and it remains unclear whether it has protective effects against AKI. PURPOSE: To investigate whether tiliroside has protective effects against AKI in mice and the associated mechanisms. METHODS: Possible tiliroside substrates were analyzed using molecular docking. Cisplatin- and ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI)-induced AKI mouse models and HK2 cells model were constructed to evaluate the protective effects of tiliroside. CRISPR/Cas9 mediated NRF2 knockout HK2 cells were used to verify whether NRF2 mediates tiliroside protective effects. RESULTS: In vivo, our results showed that tiliroside treatment preserved kidney functions in AKI mice models, as showed by lower levels of serum creatinine (SCr), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and renal injury markers, including neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and kidney injury molecule 1 (KIM1), compared with the mice in control groups. In vitro, tiliroside treatment greatly ameliorated cisplatin-induced ferroptosis through NRF2 activation in cultured HK2 cells, as evidenced by the protective effects of tiliroside being greatly blunted after the knockout of NRF2 in HK2 cells. Mechanistic studies indicated that tiliroside promoted NRF2/GPX4 pathway activation and ferroptosis inhibition, perhaps via the disruption of the NRF2-KEAP1 PPI. CONCLUSION: Together, our results demonstrate that tiliroside may serve as a NRF2-KEAP1 PPI inhibitor and prevents ferroptosis-induced AKI, indicating its potential for clinical AKI treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：铁死亡（ferroptosis）是一种依赖铁离子调控细胞死亡的过程。新近证据表明，铁死亡可促进急性肾损伤（acute kidney injury, AKI）的进展，而抑制铁死亡为AKI治疗提供了一种有效策略。NRF2-KEAP1蛋白-蛋白相互作用（protein-protein interaction, PPI）的破坏可诱导NRF2激活，这为识别新型铁死亡抑制剂提供了有前景的策略。既往研究显示，tiliroside（一种从结香（Edgeworthia chrysantha Lindl）花蕾中提取的糖苷类黄酮）通过NRF2激活发挥抗神经炎症和神经保护作用。然而，tiliroside激活NRF2的机制尚不清楚，且其对AKI是否具有保护作用仍不明确。目的：探讨tiliroside是否对小鼠AKI具有保护作用及其相关机制。方法：利用分子对接（molecular docking）分析tiliroside可能的底物。构建顺铂和缺血再灌注损伤（ischemia-reperfusion injury, IRI）诱导的AKI小鼠模型及HK2细胞模型，以评估tiliroside的保护作用。使用CRISPR/Cas9介导的NRF2敲除HK2细胞验证NRF2是否介导tiliroside的保护效应。结果：在体内实验中，我们的结果表明，与对照组小鼠相比，tiliroside处理可维持AKI小鼠模型的肾功能，表现为血清肌酐（serum creatinine, SCr）、血尿素氮（blood urea nitrogen, BUN）及肾损伤标志物（包括中性粒细胞明胶酶相关脂质运载蛋白（neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin, NGAL）和肾损伤分子1（kidney injury molecule 1, KIM1））水平降低。在体外实验中，tiliroside处理通过NRF2激活显著改善培养的HK2细胞中顺铂诱导的铁死亡，这通过HK2细胞中NRF2敲除后tiliroside的保护作用大幅减弱得到证实。机制研究表明，tiliroside可能通过破坏NRF2-KEAP1 PPI，促进NRF2/GPX4通路激活并抑制铁死亡。结论：综合来看，我们的结果表明，tiliroside可作为NRF2-KEAP1 PPI抑制剂，并预防铁死亡诱导的AKI，提示其在临床AKI治疗中具有潜在应用价值。
